target_customer: Urban commuters paying per ride for scheduled van routes, plus employers buying enterprise shuttle routes
problem: Commuters in dense cities had slow, crowded or missing transit on key corridors, while private shuttles were limited to a few employers.
business_model: Per-ride fares on fixed 15-seat van routes booked in an app, later enterprise shuttle contracts

founders.name: Ali Vahabzadeh
prior_employers: A real-estate start-up (name not given in source)
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by Wikipedia; the YC page lists only Romain Di Vuolo.

founders.name: Romain Di Vuolo
prior_employers: A real-estate start-up (name not given in source)
founders.background_notes: Listed as the founder on the YC page, which gives no background.

exit.reason: Acquired. Ford later announced on 2019-01-10 that it would shut Chariot down because the business was not sustainable.

competitors.name: Leap Transit
competitors.what: Private San Francisco commuter bus with an app, Lombard Express line
competitors.traction_then: Launched service around March 2015 at $6 per ride

competitors.name: Loup
competitors.what: Private San Francisco commuter shuttle service

technical_complexity.rationale: Chariot ran vans on fixed routes with an app for booking. The hard parts were operations, permits and route planning, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Routes, vans and drivers were rentable and copyable. Rivals Leap and Loup entered the same San Francisco market at the same time.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Ford bought Chariot in September 2016 and shut it in early 2019 as unsustainable.

market_need_then: San Francisco commuters faced crowded transit and the city was regulating private commuter shuttles in 2014 and 2015, which signaled strong demand for commute alternatives.

identity.voice_and_tone: Trademark filings include the taglines YOUR CHARIOT AWAITS and ROLL WITH CHARIOT

branding.brand_signature: Taglines Your Chariot Awaits and Roll With Chariot

brand_strength.rationale: Only trademark records and generic news coverage were found. No source shows brand-driven growth or community.

outcome_analysis: Chariot grew from a 2014 San Francisco commuter van service to nine cities and London, raised about 3 million dollars in seed funding in 2015 and sold to Ford for a reported 65 million dollars in September 2016. Ford shut it in early 2019 after judging the model not sustainable, which points to weak unit economics in microtransit. The shutdown happened under Ford ownership, so it is coded unit_economics plus other.
notes: No company website (dead site, field empty in directory). Seed details (amount, investors, April 2015) came from a search summary plus a Business Insider URL and were not seen in a primary release. Some reports say Ford paid more than 65 million dollars. Aggregators list about 3.12 million total raised. Competitors Bridj and others emerged or were documented later and are not listed.
